title: Average entropy of Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori random state ensemble
abstract: Random states play a foundational role in different branches of modern quantum science. In this work, we study a recently proposed random state ensemble induced from von Neumann entropy through the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori (BKM) metric. In particular, we derive an exact yet explicit formula of average entanglement entropy over BKM ensemble. In obtaining the formula, we only make use of properties of normalization constant of the ensemble in the absence of its correlation kernel, contrary to average entropy computation of other ensembles. This new framework paves the way for calculating higher-order cumulants of BKM ensemble beyond the average.
summary: This work develops a theoretical framework to calculate the average entanglement entropy for various random state ensembles, focusing on the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori (BKM) ensemble. By deriving an exact formula based on spectral moments and special functions, the authors establish quantitative relationships between different measures of quantum randomness. This advances the understanding of how geometric metrics influence entanglement quantification in quantum systems.
main_problem: The study focuses on deriving an exact, explicit formula for the average entanglement entropy of a random state ensemble induced using the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori (BKM) metric.
main_result: An exact formula for the average entanglement entropy $\mathbb{E}[S]$ over the BKM ensemble is derived, showing it generates the least average entropy among compared ensembles for finite dimensions.
method: The calculation involves deriving average spectral moments ($\mathbb{E}[R_l]$) using properties of the unconstrained ensemble and relating the average entropy $\mathbb{E}[S]$ to an induced entropy $\mathbb{E}[T]$ via a specific lemma involving polygamma functions.
model_or_system: The system is a bipartite quantum system described by an $m \times m$ density matrix $\rho$, and the entanglement measure used is the von Neumann entropy, $S = -\text{tr}(\rho \ln \rho)$. The analysis compares three random state ensembles: BKM, Hilbert-Schmidt (HS), and Bures-Hall (BH).
key_observables: Average entanglement entropy ($\mathbb{E}[S]$) and average spectral moments ($\mathbb{E}[R_l]$).
important_parameters: System dimension ($m$), parameter $\alpha$, and the related constant $\beta$.
main_assumptions: The derivation of $\mathbb{E}[R_l]$ relies only on the density function without using its correlation kernel, which is noted as a technical advance.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the calculated average entropy for HS, BH, and BKM ensembles against numerical simulation results.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing the framework of random state ensembles, deriving the normalization constant $C(\alpha)$ using Wronskian structure, calculating the average spectral moments $\mathbb{E}[R_l]$, and finally presenting the explicit formula for the average induced entropy $\mathbb{E}[T]$ (and thus $\mathbb{E}[S]$).
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical derivation of entanglement measures for random states, especially using advanced tools like polygamma functions, provides quantitative benchmarks for quantum information theory.
